response.sql: WITH g AS (SELECT link_to_major, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM member GROUP BY link_to_major), s AS (SELECT cnt, 1.0*cnt/(SELECT SUM(cnt) FROM g) AS share FROM g), a AS (SELECT AVG(share) AS avg_share FROM s) SELECT SUM(s.cnt) AS total_members, AVG(s.share) AS avg_share, AVG(s.share - a.avg_share) AS avg_excess FROM s, a WHERE s.share > a.avg_share

assumptions.assumption: Members with a missing major are those whose link_to_major is NULL. GROUP BY puts all NULLs into one group, and that group is counted like any other. Empty-string values are treated as a real, separate major id.
The average share is the unweighted mean of the group shares over all groups, including the missing-major group. Shares are not rounded.
